title: Rep. Chuck Edwards withdraws from re-election after ethics censure recommendation
dek: Rep. Chuck Edwards (R-N.C.) withdrew from his 2026 re-election campaign on August 5, 2026, two days after the House Ethics Committee recommended his censure over allegations of persistent unprofessional conduct toward two female staffers. The committee found Edwards violated the House Code of Official Conduct but found no evidence of sexual activity, propositions, or quid pro quo harassment.
author: The GoCheckMyNews Desk
key_fact: The Ethics Committee found Edwards engaged in a pattern of lavish gifts, comments on appearance, invitations to intimate dinners and vacations, and notes expressing affection toward two young female staffers, but concluded this did not violate the letter of federal sexual harassment law.
bottom_line: Edwards' exit closes a chapter but leaves open whether the full House will vote on the censure recommendation and whether such institutional action can shape electoral outcomes. Watch for how the North Carolina GOP primary and general election unfold in the seat Edwards vacated.
body: Rep. Chuck Edwards (R-N.C.), 65, announced his withdrawal from his 2026 re-election campaign on Wednesday morning, August 5, via a post on X. "After much prayer and reflection, I've decided to withdraw from my re-election campaign. I will complete my current term. Serving Western North Carolina has been the honor of my life. Thank you for your trust, prayers, and support," Edwards stated, according to NBC News.

Edwards' announcement came two days after the House Ethics Committee recommended on August 3 that the full House censure him. The bipartisan committee concluded in a 25-page report that Edwards "engaged in persistent unprofessional and inappropriate conduct towards two young female staffers" and "violated the House Code of Official Conduct by failing to adhere to the spirit of rules prohibiting sexual harassment of and unwanted advances to House staffers," per NBC News.

The committee detailed a pattern of behavior that "included providing the young women with lavish and recurrent gifts, making comments regarding their appearance and dress, inviting them to intimate dinners and vacations, sending notes regarding his effusive affection, and inviting them to other activities as a way to spend time together," according to NBC News.

However, the committee also found significant boundaries. It concluded that the allegations "do not implicate quid pro quo sexual harassment" and do not violate "the 'letter' of federal sexual harassment law," per NBC News. The panel found no evidence that Edwards engaged in sexual activity with or propositioned any staffers. Edwards denied that any of his actions were intended to be sexual or romantic in nature, and the committee reported that Edwards cooperated with the investigation.

Edwards has previously called the allegations "baseless." In May 2026, he told NBC News that he welcomed an investigation. After the committee's report, his counsel filed a 15-page rebuttal, calling the findings "unfounded," per NBC News.
Edwards defeated Rep. Madison Cawthorn in the GOP primary in 2022. His withdrawal reshapes the race for a seat in a competitive region of Western North Carolina.
